about.what: The delivery method this programme learned, held as data so the platform can apply it to its own changes instead of it living in an assistant's notes. Served by /api/v1/method. Amended ONLY through Change Control (POST /api/v1/method/derive proposes a CANDIDATE; the agency ratifies it), because the agency that checks changes against the method must also own the method.
about.why_each_row_carries_a_defect: A rule with no defect behind it is an opinion. Every lesson here names the round and the concrete failure that produced it, so a reader can judge the rule by the evidence rather than by its phrasing — and so a rule can be RETIRED when the defect it answers stops being possible.
about.what_enforced_by_means: A real tool or guard path that would CATCH a breach, or null. Null is the common case and is stated, never implied: most of this method is judgement a change record cannot expose. A gate that reported these as MET would be the exact defect this programme spent its rounds removing — a green badge over requirements nothing evaluated.
about.three_states: A method check returns MET, UNMET or NOT_ASSESSABLE with a basis. NOT_ASSESSABLE is the honest answer for any requirement whose satisfaction is not visible in the artefacts the platform holds, and it is the majority answer.
about.owner_ruling: 2026-09-27 — the rulings are the constitution. 2026-09-29 — measurement, acceptance-criteria bars, alignment to vision value and progress-to-completion belong in the method as a group of their own. 2026-09-29 (second): preparation and handover are groups of the method in their own right, and reach the Transformation Office and the Change Control Agency. 2026-09-29 (third): the written record — the knowledge operating process, the handovers and the three defect ledgers — is reviewed for methodology, and what it holds is distilled into the method rather than left in prose. 2026-09-29 (fourth): FORECASTING (how long work takes and in what order) and LEARNING (how experience, mistakes and successes become method) are groups of the method in their own right, mined from this programme's own record, and reach the Transformation Office and the Change Control Agency. 2026-09-29 (fifth): DIAGNOSING (the step between a symptom and a patch) and CORRECTING (how a wrong thing is made right without moving the defect) are groups of the method in their own right — the two steps this programme has lost the most time in, and the two the register had no rules for. 2026-09-29 (sixth): the appraisal talent — reflection to reasoning, attribution to recognition, foresight to hindsight, introspection to extrospection — is captured as a CELL, usable as diagnosis and correction are, within Workstation and reaching the Transformation Office and the Change Control Agency. 2026-09-29 (seventh): the Appraisal Cell carries a temporal SPINE — retrospection, observation, prospection — because the cognitive time-axis has a middle and the cell was built without it.
about.generated: authored W508 from the programme's own confirmed defects; amended only through Change Control
about.what_defect_classes_are: A lesson is a rule for whoever is working; a defect class is a SHAPE a screen can look for. The classes below were distilled from this repository's own defect ledgers, where each was found by sweeping for the shape rather than by reading for the rule. Each names how to find it and what the fix is, and D-FABRICATE also names what is NOT in the class, because eleven of seventy proposals were legitimately defended.
about.what_breaches_are: A breach is an occasion on which a rule was broken AFTER it was written. Breaches are NOT recorded in this document: it is amended only through Change Control, so they live in their own operational store (data/method_breaches.json) and GET /api/v1/method joins the count in at read time. A count of zero means no breach has been RECORDED, which is not a statement that none happened — nothing observes a breach. The third recorded breach of a lesson nothing enforces raises a Change Control candidate, because a rule broken after being written needs a tool rather than a reminder (M-LEARN-02, M-LEARN-03).
about.what_a_cell_is: Most groups in this register are lists of rules an operator follows. APPRAISAL is a CELL: a reusable unit that takes a scope and produces eight readings over it, in four paired axes, where neither end of an axis is sufficient alone. It is named for the organism's functional unit because that is what it is — the faculties are its organelles, and it can be run by the Transformation Office over a transformation's scope or by Change Control over a change's, as well as over the delivery plan itself. Its structures are FOUR AXES of two ends each and ONE SPINE of three: an axis is a dyad whose ends check each other, a spine is a triad whose middle is the present. The Owner's cognitive map is the source of the spine — Past ↔ Present ↔ Future, Memory ↔ Perception ↔ Imagination, Learning ↔ Orientation ↔ Planning.

lessons.rule: A concept is not delivered until something the user reaches is different. Frame every item by the surface that changes, not by the component that gets built.
lessons.defect: W446–W505: nine cognitive engines, a five-gate clearance chain, a reflex mechanism and a delivery-check classification all EXISTED and none of them ran. Each had been built to a component description rather than to a reachable surface, so 'built' and 'reached' diverged silently for rounds.
lessons.apply: State the item's deliverable as a surface a person or a caller meets. If the item can be finished without any surface changing, it is a component, and the item is not done.
lessons.why_not_enforced: No artefact distinguishes a wired component from an unwired one; reachability needs a dotted-import check AND a same-package relative check AND a runtime-scan check, and even all three missed a case (W482).

lessons.rule: Deliver the whole of what the Owner described. Do not sample a vision and build the sample.
lessons.defect: The Owner's mandate, recorded after a round delivered a subset of a brief and reported it as the brief. The fine-resolution vision now lives in docs/WORKSTATION_IDBO_WHOLE_VISION.md precisely so a round cannot quietly narrow it.
lessons.apply: Before building from a brief, interrogate it into items and state what each item does NOT cover. A narrowing is a decision and belongs to the Owner.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Scope fidelity is a judgement against a document, not a property of a diff.

lessons.rule: Order work by vision value, not by what is easy or recent.
lessons.defect: Rounds were choosing rows by recency, so low-value rows closed while high-value ones aged. W478 introduced scoring by vision value.
lessons.apply: Start a round from `python scripts/followups.py priority`, which ranks open rows by tier, area and reach from docs/PRIORITY.json.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/followups.py priority

lessons.rule: A round's unit is a file-connected component cut by item, not a list of unrelated rows.
lessons.defect: W503 closed ten rows and ZERO items, because the rows were scattered across items and none of them completed an item's bar. Closing rows is not progress if no item can close.
lessons.apply: `python scripts/followups.py bundles` computes the file-connected subsystem; `batches` computes the class one mechanism closes. Take one, not a scatter.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/row_components.py

lessons.rule: A batch generator that cannot see a row has a blind spot, and the blind spot is part of the tool.
lessons.defect: The class-batch generator groups rows by a cited defect class and therefore cannot see a row that cites none. That limitation is declared rather than discovered later.
lessons.apply: When a batch looks small, check whether rows without a class were simply invisible to the generator before concluding there is little to do.
lessons.why_not_enforced: A tool cannot detect what it is structurally unable to see; only a reader comparing the batch against the full open set can.

lessons.rule: An item closes on its ACCEPT bar. No bar means UNEXAMINED, never nearly done.
lessons.defect: W505: no P2 item had closed in 48 rounds while 32 rows closed in six, because 17 of 48 open build items stated NO acceptance clause — there was nothing to check them against. Nothing had been forgotten; the bar did not exist.
lessons.apply: An item whose body lists deliverables does not need a bar invented: the deliverables ARE the bar, and writing them as ACCEPT is transcription plus a guard. A round that finishes an item's work must write its bar if it has none, or the work cannot be recognised.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Whether a bar's clauses match an item's body is a reading, not a parse. An audit can count items with no bar at all; it cannot judge a bar's fidelity.

lessons.rule: Write the bar against the DEFECT, never against correct output. A criterion satisfied by the thing being fixed is not a criterion.
lessons.defect: W505 found four acceptance criteria worded so that correct output satisfied them, so the item could be 'met' without the defect being fixed.
lessons.apply: For each clause ask: what state of the code makes this FALSE? If nothing does, the clause is decorative.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Judging whether a clause can fail requires reasoning about the code it describes.

lessons.rule: A count states the population it covers. A figure with no stated denominator is not a measurement.
lessons.defect: W491: a `kind` field describing what a resource IS was read by five counters to say what HAPPENED, so every failed attempt counted as a run or a read — 31 of 47 findings in one round were this shape.
lessons.apply: Name the population in the field or beside it. 'Assessable' and 'exists' are different denominators, and a fall-through is not a reading.
lessons.why_not_enforced: A count's intended population is not recoverable from the count.

lessons.rule: Project progress in ROUNDS, never in dates. State the rate's population and name the weakest number on the page.
lessons.defect: W486/W499: a projection was an average over a population most of which no round had measured. Stating it as a date would have invented a promise; stating it without its weakness would have hidden one.
lessons.apply: Measure the rate from the register, project in rounds, exclude one-time sweeps by name, and refuse to project where too few rounds have closed one of an item's rows. Say which figure is weakest and why.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/followups.py forecast

lessons.rule: Two rates, and only one is the lever: rows closed and ITEMS closed. Report both and act on the item rate.
lessons.defect: W503 closed ten rows and no item, and the row rate made the round look productive. The item rate is what moves the plan.
lessons.apply: Report rows/round and items/round separately, over their own populations, and choose the next round by which items can actually close.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/followups.py forecast

lessons.rule: A measurement row that OVERSTATES a problem is the same defect as one that understates it.
lessons.defect: W505: a row asserted '17 of 48 items state no bar' and used the stale figure in its own reasoning before re-checking it. Six of the seventeen had since been barred or closed.
lessons.apply: Re-measure before citing your own earlier measurement. A figure in a register row ages.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Staleness is only visible by re-running the measurement the row describes.

lessons.rule: Measure each row's LIVE state before building. A row may accuse working code.
lessons.defect: W507: FU-241 and FU-244 both claimed a script walked a directory it does not walk; every traversal root was a named top-level directory. Building the 'fix' would have changed correct code on a false premise. Earlier, W502: a blind was vacuous because a two-argument constructor was called with one, the TypeError was swallowed, and the branch never ran — trusting it would have 'fixed' correct code.
lessons.apply: Read the code the row names before writing anything. If the row's claim is false, DROP the row with the measurement that refutes it.
lessons.why_not_enforced: A row's truth is established by reading the code it points at.

lessons.rule: Fix the CLASS once, at the chokepoint — and grep the CALL, not the method name.
lessons.defect: W489: a 'repo-wide' audit checked one of four entry points and missed 29 callers. W507: the posting-source tag went on `_apply_posting` rather than `post`, because a caller reached the former directly and tagging the latter would have left every inter-VSB debit untagged.
lessons.apply: Find every entry point before choosing where to fix. Flip the DEFAULT rather than editing call sites where the default is the defect.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Identifying the true chokepoint is a reading of the call graph.

lessons.rule: Every writer, the reached surface, and an executing guard leg must all say the new truth.
lessons.defect: W475 found 25 misses of exactly this. W507 repeated it twice in one round: a second copy of a retired control in the other render path, and a field written to a store that the reader dropped so it was rendered nowhere.
lessons.apply: After a truth fix, enumerate the writers, the readers and the surfaces. A writer fixed without its reader just moves the lie down a layer.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/selfcheck_diff.py (the keys and renames checks catch a key no consumer reads, and a key removed while readers survive)

lessons.rule: A field's meaning belongs to its readers. ADD a field; never re-point an existing one.
lessons.defect: W495: re-pointing a stored `success` field at a quality verdict broke model routing, model health and a status route — six of nine suite failures. W507 followed the rule deliberately: the venture funding figures were added beside `invested_total` rather than changing what it meant.
lessons.apply: Grep the readers before changing what a word means. If readers exist, add.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/selfcheck_diff.py (renames)

lessons.rule: Removing a true statement is also a defect.
lessons.defect: W502: narrowing an over-claim killed a case where the strong statement was TRUE.
lessons.apply: When downgrading a claim, check the cases where it held, and carry its consequences across rather than deleting them.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Whether a removed statement was true in some case is a reading of that case.

lessons.rule: Register every found-but-not-done task in the same commit, slotted to a plan item.
lessons.defect: W462: work found mid-round and not written down was lost between rounds, so the same defects were rediscovered.
lessons.apply: `python scripts/followups.py add` in the same commit. Close or reslot an item's riders BEFORE marking it done — the suite fails on a row left on a finished item.
lessons.enforced_by: integration_tests/test_mvp_spine.py::test_w462_followup_register_is_scheduled_and_in_lockstep

lessons.rule: When a row's fix reads 'do X OR Y', it is an Owner decision whatever its slot says. Surface it; do not pick.
lessons.defect: W507: the register formally counted ONE row awaiting the Owner while three more carried embedded either/or choices slotted to build items — so decisions the Owner should have made were about to be taken by whoever happened to reach the row.
lessons.apply: Slot such a row OWNER so the plan counts it, and state the options with the measurement behind each.
lessons.enforced_by: integration_tests/test_mvp_spine.py (an OWNER row must carry the owner-gated flag and say why it is one)

lessons.rule: Green is evidence only if red was reachable. Make every new instrument fail first.
lessons.defect: W498–W500: three instruments that could not fail reported success — a watcher whose pattern pytest never prints (it slept four hours), a leak assertion over a surface designed not to propagate it, and a sweep reporting off an absent test where exit code 5 read as a pass.
lessons.apply: Break the thing, watch the guard fail, restore. A harness must distinguish BAD BLIND (the anchor did not match) from VACUOUS (the guard stayed green with its subject broken), and must abort on a selector that matched no test.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Only running the blind proves the guard can fail; no artefact records that it was run.

lessons.rule: A guard must DRIVE its precondition, never observe the ambient environment.
lessons.defect: W493: five of seven checks were defective because they observed whatever the environment happened to be — a dirty tree, a one-outcome exit code, a negative narrowed away by split(), an `or []` that hid the case. W507: a revert leg read the lever's current value, so a revert that restored NOTHING satisfied it until the leg set the value first.
lessons.apply: Set the state the guard needs, assert the precondition took, then assert the behaviour.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Whether a guard drives or observes is a property of its logic, not of its text.

lessons.rule: Assert the CONDITION, not the message. And a guard cannot search its own file.
lessons.defect: W491: 17 of 79 blinds were vacuous because an assertion containing the literal it forbids or requires matches itself. W503: nine of 46 vacuous, five of them one class — a JSX conditional names its field in the gate AND the body, so a presence check survives `{false && ...}`.
lessons.apply: Check the field, the binding or the AST — never the source text. A presence check cannot see a disabled gate.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/selfcheck_diff.py (selfmatch: a test assertion that matches its own text)

lessons.rule: A fix comment must not quote the literal its own guard forbids or requires.
lessons.defect: W495: five red runs because the comment recording a removal quoted the phrase its guard forbids. W507 did it AGAIN, twice: a comment explaining the recall disclosure contained the literal a guard grepped for, and a comment naming two fields let a presence check pass after the real binding was deleted.
lessons.apply: Forbid the BINDING or the RENDER, and put the old wording in the commit message. If a guard greps text, that is the guard's defect — convert it to an AST check.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/selfcheck_diff.py (banned: a comment quoting a literal a guard forbids)

lessons.rule: A basis string is code. Compute a claim from state; never assert a universal in prose.
lessons.defect: W494: 32 of 76 confirmed findings were basis sentences asserting universals instead of computing them — 'cannot fall below 0.6' written over a blend measured at 0.472. W507: a basis said an energy figure never depletes 'because it is floored at 0.5', and the floor never binds; the real reason is that production exceeds consumption fourfold.
lessons.apply: Derive every basis from the values it describes, so it corrects itself when they change. A declared domain nobody enforces is not a domain.
lessons.why_not_enforced: This is the largest unenforced class (30 of 98 in the labelled set); FU-262 proposes extending the pre-flight to it.

lessons.rule: Refute the round's OWN fix before shipping it, as hard as the code it changed.
lessons.defect: W488: 25 of 29 verified findings were the round's own defect class re-committed INSIDE its own fix. W493: the round's new instrument was itself defective in five of seven checks.
lessons.apply: Run the adversarial pass over the diff the round just produced, including its guard legs, not only over the code it touched.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Adversarial refutation is a process; the artefacts do not record that it ran.

lessons.rule: A stub must not be thinner than its producer.
lessons.defect: W506 added a `source` argument to a ledger writer; a test stub kept the old signature, so the cycle raised 'unexpected keyword argument' and the test read that as the ledger failure it was simulating.
lessons.apply: Match the producer's signature explicitly. Do NOT absorb new arguments into **kwargs: a stub that silently swallows them stops reporting that the producer changed, and that report is worth a red run.
lessons.why_not_enforced: A stub's fidelity to its producer is not checkable without executing both.

lessons.rule: A guard that cannot find its subject must FAIL, not pass.
lessons.defect: W507: a guard leg named a handler that does not exist and wrote `if not fn: continue`, so it silently checked nothing for the one path whose lock most needed proving.
lessons.apply: Assert the subject was found before asserting anything about it.
lessons.why_not_enforced: A skipped branch looks identical to a satisfied one in a passing run.

lessons.rule: Verify a route by CALLING it. A boot is not a call.
lessons.defect: A helper inserted between a @router decorator and its handler silently rebinds the route, which 422s only when called. W492 then had three guards stay green over it — one imported the helper, one counted source occurrences, and one checked for a 422 that passed because everything 422'd.
lessons.apply: Never place a definition between a decorator and its handler. Assert the AST binding AND call the route.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/selfcheck_diff.py (routes: a route decorator bound to a private helper)

lessons.rule: Three-state verdicts. NOT ASSESSABLE is an answer, and usually the honest one.
lessons.defect: Repeatedly across W436–W494: a boolean coerced with bool() meant a check that examined nothing could only report success. A screen that can refuse and escalate but cannot clear must never report a pass.
lessons.apply: True (a real check ran and passed) · False (a real check ran and failed) · None (nothing real was checked), each with a basis saying which.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Whether a check is real is a property of what it examines.

lessons.rule: Use a FRESH store for every verification run, and never two suites at once.
lessons.defect: Two concurrent suites once produced ~40 false failures on shared stores. W507 lost two full suite runs in one night: one to a mid-run deletion of the suite's own data directory, one to running other pytest invocations beside it (four hours of wall clock for 355 seconds of CPU).
lessons.apply: Isolate DATA_DIR, WORKSTATION_DATA_DIR, WORKSTATION_UEG_PATH and PROJECTS_DIR per run. Touch nothing while a suite runs.
lessons.enforced_by: integration_tests/conftest.py (per-worker store isolation) and integration_tests/test_xdist_iso.py

lessons.rule: A platform may only report what it did.
lessons.defect: The founding defect of this programme, in every shape: invented citations written to a knowledge base as INGESTED; a hard-coded scripture rendering presented as a user's file content; a SHA3 digest with a built-in key stamped as a post-quantum signature; positions recorded against named entities that were never credited.
lessons.apply: Every figure, verdict and badge names what produced it. Where nothing produced it, say that instead.
lessons.why_not_enforced: This is the whole method's purpose, not a single checkable property.

lessons.rule: The qualifier travels WITH the figure — into the download, the server export, the file on disk and the card footer.
lessons.defect: W490: provenance was added to a page and the download still shipped unlabelled. W507: a controller published an energy figure while dropping the measured flag and basis its own source had carried since W494, so every surface below it printed a simulator as a live vital.
lessons.apply: A badge in the DOM is not a label on the text. Follow the value to every place it is rendered or written.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/selfcheck_diff.py (keys: a key produced and read by no surface)

lessons.rule: A row closes only when EVERY finding in it is fixed. Partial is open.
lessons.defect: Rows were closed on their headline while their body listed further findings, so the register reported progress the code did not have.
lessons.apply: Read the row's whole body before closing. If part is done, close nothing and register the remainder as its own row.
lessons.why_not_enforced: A row's completeness is a reading of its body against the diff.

lessons.rule: Preserve each file's line endings, and commit with an explicit file list.
lessons.defect: `sed -i` rewrote a CRLF file as LF on a no-match. `git add -A` swept unrelated renames into one commit and silently skipped a gitignored file CI needed. W507: a heredoc wrote an LF line into a CRLF file, leaving it mixed.
lessons.apply: Check `git ls-files --eol` before and after. Convert every needle to the file's own ending. Name every file in the commit.
lessons.why_not_enforced: An EOL flip is visible in `git ls-files --eol` but nothing runs it automatically; a candidate for the pre-flight.

lessons.rule: Assert every scripted replacement. An unasserted edit that matches nothing ships silently.
lessons.defect: A scripted str.replace missed on a CRLF mismatch and shipped a fabricated-success button through a whole round, because nothing checked that the replacement had happened.
lessons.apply: Assert the anchor matches exactly once before replacing, and re-parse afterwards. Prefer an editing tool for load-bearing changes.
lessons.why_not_enforced: The assertion lives in the patch script, which is not itself an artefact of the change.

lessons.rule: Ask the archive before building. A cleanup that MOVED work is invisible to a delete-only search.
lessons.defect: W482: 516 files had been moved into _archive/ and 3 deleted, so searches for deletions found almost nothing and work was rebuilt that already existed.
lessons.apply: Run `python scripts/recovery_audit.py` first. Recover the SHAPE of archived work, never a simulated corpus.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/recovery_audit.py

lessons.rule: Correct an over-claim you made yourself, in the same round, in the record.
lessons.defect: W507: the plan was written to say a new assessor makes the overall compliance verdict reachable. Building it showed the verdict stays unreachable until every framework has an assessor. The claim was corrected in the plan and the memory rather than left standing.
lessons.apply: When the build contradicts the plan's own words, change the words. A stronger claim that survives because nobody re-read it is the same defect as one that was never checked.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Only a reader comparing the plan's claim against the built behaviour can see it.

lessons.rule: Preparation is MEASUREMENT, not planning. Read the live state of every row before building anything from it.
lessons.defect: W507-W508, in one session: two rows (FU-241, FU-244) claimed a script walked a directory it does not walk and were DROPPED as false; two more (FU-247, FU-261) were already satisfied and merely open; and a fifth (FU-248) was three-quarters done. Building any of them from the row's text would have changed correct code on a false premise.
lessons.apply: For each row, read the code it names and record what is actually there. A row that is false is DROPPED with the measurement that refutes it; a row already satisfied is CLOSED. Neither is a build.
lessons.why_not_enforced: A row's truth is established by reading the code it points at; no artefact records whether that was done.

lessons.rule: Prepare the BAR before the build. An item with no acceptance criteria cannot be closed however much is built.
lessons.defect: W505: no P2 item closed in 48 rounds while 32 rows closed in six, because 17 of 48 open build items stated no acceptance clause. W508 measured the same in Phase 3: ELEVEN of 26 items state none, so eleven cannot be closed as written whatever is delivered.
lessons.apply: An item whose body lists deliverables does not need a bar invented - the deliverables ARE the bar, and writing them as ACCEPT is transcription plus a guard. Write it before or with the work, never after.
lessons.why_not_enforced: An audit can count items with no bar at all; whether a bar's clauses match its item's body is a reading.

lessons.rule: Prepare a patch as a script whose every anchor is ASSERTED, and whose needles carry the target file's own line endings.
lessons.defect: A scripted replace missed on a CRLF mismatch and shipped a fabricated-success button through a whole round, because nothing checked the replacement happened. W507-W508 hit the line-ending half four separate times: an LF needle matches nothing in a CRLF file, silently, and one heredoc left a CRLF file MIXED.
lessons.apply: Assert every anchor matches exactly once, convert every needle to the file's own ending, re-parse afterwards, and check `git ls-files --eol` before and after. Prefer an editing tool for load-bearing changes; a heredoc eats escapes.
lessons.why_not_enforced: The assertion lives in the patch script, which is not an artefact of the change. An EOL flip IS visible in `git ls-files --eol` and is a candidate for the pre-flight.

lessons.rule: Prepare during dead time, but READ-ONLY. Never touch the tree or a running verification's store.
lessons.defect: W507 lost TWO full 50-minute suite runs in one night: one to deleting the suite's own data directory mid-run, and one to running other pytest invocations beside it - four hours of wall clock for 355 seconds of CPU.
lessons.apply: While a suite runs: read files, measure, and write prepared patches to a scratchpad. Apply nothing. A prepared patch applied after green costs a minute; a corrupted run costs the round.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Nothing observes what else is running; the discipline is the operator's.

lessons.rule: Ask the archive before building. A cleanup that MOVED work is invisible to a delete-only search.
lessons.defect: W482: 516 files had been moved into _archive/ and only 3 deleted, so searches for deletions found almost nothing and work was rebuilt that already existed.
lessons.apply: Run `python scripts/recovery_audit.py` first. Recover the SHAPE of archived work, never a simulated corpus - 342 archived rows read 'Simulated content for <filename>' and were stamped EXTRACTED.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/recovery_audit.py

lessons.rule: Name what the round will NOT do, before it starts.
lessons.defect: The Owner's standing mandate, recorded after a round delivered a subset of a brief and reported it as the brief. W508 applied it in the other direction: P2.8's five criteria were all built and the item was NOT closed, because two rows still rode it - and saying so was the deliverable.
lessons.apply: State the excluded scope explicitly when proposing a round, and again when reporting it. A narrowing is a decision and belongs to the Owner.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Scope fidelity is a judgement against a document.

lessons.rule: A WORKING CONTEXT ENDS. Only the register, the plan and the memory survive it - never the conversation.
lessons.defect: This programme's own sessions are compacted mid-flight. Everything that carried across did so because it was written to docs/FOLLOWUPS.json, the plan, or a memory file; everything held only in the exchange was gone. A round that 'remembers' a decision has not recorded it.
lessons.apply: Before a context ends, and continuously rather than at the end: every found-but-not-done task is a register row, every ruling is in the plan, and every durable lesson is in this method. If it matters after the context, it is in an artefact.
lessons.enforced_by: integration_tests/test_mvp_spine.py::test_w462_followup_register_is_scheduled_and_in_lockstep

lessons.rule: Hand over the MEASUREMENT, not the conclusion. A figure ages; the method that produced it can be re-run.
lessons.defect: W505: a row asserted '17 of 48 items state no bar' and used the stale figure in its own reasoning before re-checking it - six of the seventeen had since been barred or closed. W508 found a row still claiming '19 call sites' where the real count was 1.
lessons.apply: Record HOW a figure was measured, so a successor can re-measure rather than inherit. A measurement row that overstates a problem is the same defect as one that understates it.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Staleness is only visible by re-running the measurement the row describes.

lessons.rule: State plainly what is UNVERIFIED, and what was left out and why.
lessons.defect: W507 reported a 4.8x suite speedup that was real and then found it stalled one run in three with no established cause. Banking the win would have handed a successor a tool that fails silently a third of the time - the instrument-that-cannot-fail defect inverted.
lessons.apply: A handover names: what is verified and by which guard, what is built but unverified, what is measured but unexplained, and what was deliberately not done. A green figure with an unstated caveat is worse than no figure.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Whether a caveat was stated is a reading of the report.

lessons.rule: Every open DECISION is slotted to the Owner so the plan counts it. 'Do X or Y' is never a build.
lessons.defect: W507: the register formally counted ONE row awaiting the Owner while three more (FU-167, FU-260, FU-256b) carried embedded either/or choices slotted to build items - so decisions the Owner should have made were about to be taken by whoever next reached the row.
lessons.apply: Slot such a row OWNER, state the options with the measurement behind each, and do not pick. An OWNER row must carry the owner-gated flag and say why it is one.
lessons.enforced_by: integration_tests/test_mvp_spine.py (an OWNER-slotted row must carry the flag and a slot_source)

lessons.rule: Hand over the INSTRUMENTS: which guards exist, which blinds were run, and which came back vacuous and why.
lessons.defect: W491: 17 of 79 blinds were vacuous. W503: 9 of 46, five of them one class. W508: two vacuous blinds were each a real guard weakness - a substring match with no boundary, and a check satisfied by any one of three references. A successor who is told only 'the guards pass' inherits the weakness with the guard.
lessons.apply: Report the blind count, the red count, and every vacuous result with its cause. A vacuous blind is a finding about the guard, not a formality.
lessons.why_not_enforced: No artefact records that a blind sweep ran or what it found.

lessons.rule: Correct the round's own over-claims IN THE RECORD before handing over, not in the next conversation.
lessons.defect: W507 wrote into the plan that a new assessor made the overall compliance verdict reachable. Building it showed the verdict stays unreachable until every framework has an assessor. The plan and the memory were corrected in the same round; left standing, a successor would have inherited the stronger claim as fact.
lessons.apply: When the build contradicts the plan's own words, change the words. A claim that survives because nobody re-read it is the same defect as one that was never checked.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Only a reader comparing the record against the built behaviour can see it.

lessons.rule: The vision PREVAILS. Where the live system differs from it, the difference is the work to do — never a redefinition of the vision down to what exists.
lessons.defect: docs/KNOWLEDGE_OPERATING_PROCESS.md §1 records this as the rule of coherence over five layers (vision, understanding, plan, memory, code) after the layers had drifted: a plan reconciled to capability reads as coherent and has quietly deleted scope. The Owner's standing mandate names the same failure from the other side — a round that delivered a subset of a brief and reported it as the brief.
lessons.apply: When a document and the tree disagree, change whichever one is WRONG, and a vision is wrong only when the Owner says so. Code/live state is ground truth about what EXISTS; it is never ground truth about what was asked for. A gap becomes a plan item, not an edit to the brief.
lessons.why_not_enforced: A fidelity audit can score section-by-section coverage (scripts/workflows/fidelity_audit_v3.js), but whether a rewording narrowed intent is a reading.

lessons.rule: DECOMPOSE a backlog line before working it. A line that names a count rather than its contents hides what doing it would ship.
lessons.defect: docs/NATIVE_PRIMITIVE_DEFECT_LEDGER.md: the backlog said '10 unreached native-AI routes', which reads as wiring work. Decomposing it first found that NINE of the ten carried a fabrication-class defect, so working the line as written would have shipped nine misleading surfaces in one change. The ledger's own words: decomposing the backlog before working it is what caught this.
lessons.apply: Expand a counted line into its members and read each one before scheduling it. A line whose members have never been looked at is UNEXAMINED — the same state M-MEAS-01 names for an item with no bar, and it estimates the same way: not at all.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Whether a line was expanded before being worked leaves no trace in an artefact.

lessons.rule: Order fixes by REACHABILITY. A defect in code nothing reaches is a ledger entry, not an incident — and inflating one into the other spends the attention the reachable ones need.
lessons.defect: docs/NATIVE_PRIMITIVE_DEFECT_LEDGER.md audited one entry in depth — including measuring how badly noise outweighed its signal — before anyone asked whether it runs. It does not. docs/FABRICATION_LEDGER.md states the converse as its working order: 63 surviving findings fixed top-down by reachability, 'what a user actually sees comes first'.
lessons.apply: Ask whether a finding is reached BEFORE auditing it deeply, and record the reach beside it. Then fix in reach order. This does not mean unreached defects are ignored: they are recorded as latent, which is what a ledger is for. Note the trap in the other direction — [[feedback-reachability-blind-spots]] — imports and a green suite do not prove a file is unreached, because infra-only references and runtime directory scans reach code no import graph shows.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/reach_audit.py

lessons.rule: A screen states what it does NOT flag. An exclusion list is part of the instrument, and a screen without one reports noise as findings.
lessons.defect: docs/FABRICATION_LEDGER.md: 70 findings proposed, ELEVEN successfully DEFENDED, 63 surviving. The defended eleven were configuration constants, clearly-labelled fallbacks, test fixtures, archived files, honest empty states and prompt/example text — none of which is a fabrication. Without that list written down, a re-run of the same sweep re-proposes them, and the operator re-adjudicates eleven settled cases to reach the real 63.
lessons.apply: Every screen carries its scope AND its exclusions, and an adversarial DEFENCE pass runs before the findings are treated as findings. A proposal that is defended is recorded as defended — not deleted — so the next sweep inherits the adjudication.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Whether an exclusion is legitimate or a convenient escape is exactly the judgement the defence pass exists to make.

lessons.rule: Identical failure lines across different blinds mean the RUN was contaminated, not that the blinds were caught.
lessons.defect: docs/HANDOVER_W470.md §3 records this as a rhythm rule after a break run reported every blind red. They were red for one shared reason — a dirty tree or a corrupted store — so the sweep proved nothing about any guard. It is the instrument-that-cannot-fail defect (M-VERIF-01) inverted: an instrument that cannot PASS is equally uninformative.
lessons.apply: Read the failure LINES, not the red count. Distinct blinds must fail for distinct reasons, at the assertion each one targets. Byte-restore from a captured copy, never with a checkout, and separate BAD BLIND (the edit did not compile) from VACUOUS (the guard never saw it).
lessons.why_not_enforced: No artefact records that a blind sweep ran, let alone which line each blind failed at.

lessons.rule: A shared record has ONE writer, and it must add up against itself. A record that miscounts its own table is the same defect class as the code it documents.
lessons.defect: docs/NATIVE_PRIMITIVE_DEFECT_LEDGER.md: a status section said '5 fixed + 4 open' over a table of NINE, with `entropy` in neither list — it was still open, and was found only because someone re-added the table. docs/HANDOVER_W470.md §5.4 records the writer half: the register and the plan move together and only through scripts/followups.py; editing PLAN NOW by hand fails the suite, as does an open row sitting where its routes would not send it, or a finished item still carrying a row.
lessons.apply: Change the register and the plan through their tool, never by hand. Re-add every summary against the rows it summarises — a total, a status split and a table are three chances to disagree, and a summary nobody re-added is a claim nobody checked.
lessons.enforced_by: integration_tests/test_mvp_spine.py (the register/plan lockstep legs) + scripts/followups.py check

lessons.rule: Forecast the ITEM, never the row. Rows closing is motion; items closing is progress toward completion, and the two can point opposite ways.
lessons.defect: Measured at W505: 32 rows closed across six rounds while ZERO Phase 2 items closed in FORTY-EIGHT. A row-based reading said the plan was moving at ten rows a round; the plan had not advanced by a single item. W503 is the clearest single round — ten rows closed, no item.
lessons.apply: Report both rates and project from the item rate. The row rate sizes a ROUND; the item rate sizes the PLAN. Measure the item rate over the whole span rather than a six-round window, because a window cannot measure something that takes many rounds.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/plan_followups.py forecast() — reports both rates and projects on items

lessons.rule: The open-row count is an UPPER BOUND on remaining work, not a measure of it. Re-read the rows before forecasting from them.
lessons.defect: Three consecutive rounds, measured: W507 DROPPED two rows (FU-241, FU-244) as factually false — the script they accused walks no such path; W508 found two already satisfied (FU-247, FU-261) and a third three-quarters done (FU-248); W509 measured P2.8's six open rows and FIVE were already satisfied by earlier rounds and had simply never been closed. Roughly nine of the last fifteen rows examined needed no build at all, so a projection off open rows is biased HIGH by a large and unstable factor.
lessons.apply: Re-read the rows; never apply a correction factor to the count. A row measured false is DROPPED with the measurement that refutes it, and a row already satisfied is CLOSED — both are forecasting work, and both make the projection more honest rather than shorter.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Whether a row is still true is a reading of the code it names. A tool can surface CANDIDATES — open rows whose files a later round changed — and that instrument does not exist yet.

lessons.rule: Budget the VERIFICATION, not the patch. The cost of a round is dominated by proving the change, not by making it.
lessons.defect: Measured on this programme: a round's patch is minutes of work, while the full suite is about fifty minutes and must run ONCE on the final tree; a blind sweep is one run per blind, and two rounds ran 79 and 46 of them; adversarial refutation took six to eight passes to converge. A forecast built from the size of the diff is wrong by an order of magnitude, and every schedule this programme has overrun was overrun here.
lessons.apply: Size a round as: the patch, plus one full suite on the final tree, plus one run per blind, plus the refutation passes. When the verification cost exceeds the patch cost by that much, the lever is FEWER, LARGER rounds over one file-connected component — not faster patching.
lessons.why_not_enforced: No artefact records how long a round's verification took; the commit gaps in git are wall clock and include everything else (M-FCAST-04).

lessons.rule: Wall clock is not work. Report the VARIANCE and its cause, never the median alone — the long tail is rework, and rework is preventable in a way that work is not.
lessons.defect: Two measurements, side by side. Git: 32 commit-to-commit gaps, median 4.5 hours per round, range 0.2 to 10.9 — a spread of fifty-fold that a median conceals entirely. And one night inside that range spent FOUR HOURS of wall clock for 355 seconds of CPU, because two full suite runs were destroyed — one by deleting the suite's own data directory mid-run, one by running other pytest invocations beside it.
lessons.apply: Quote the range with the median, and separate rework from work when you can name it. A forecast that hides a fifty-fold spread behind a central figure is a promise. The two lost runs were self-inflicted and are governed by M-PREP-04, which is why the discipline and the forecast belong in the same register.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/followups.py forecast — the WALL CLOCK line reports the median with its range

lessons.rule: Order by what UNBLOCKS, then by value. An item held behind another cannot be closed by working it, however high it scores.
lessons.defect: Measured at W508: P2.11-P2.16 are held behind P3.12-P3.19 by the Owner's ruling, because a membrane in front of machinery that does not run can only be verified against its absence. So PHASE 2 CANNOT CLOSE BEFORE A CHUNK OF PHASE 3, and no amount of row-closing inside Phase 2 changes that. A schedule ordered purely by priority score would have worked six items that cannot complete.
lessons.apply: Resolve the blocking order first, then order the unblocked set by vision value (docs/PRIORITY.json). State the gate in the schedule so it is visible rather than rediscovered: at W508 the gate is P3.12, and nothing above it moves first.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/plan_followups.py _gate_phase() — the gate phase bounds the schedule

lessons.rule: The unit bounds the estimate. A round is one file-connected component cut by ONE item — not a count of rows.
lessons.defect: W503 closed ten rows and zero items, which is the measured ceiling of what row-cutting achieves. A round spanning unrelated files pays the whole verification cost once per cluster and converges more slowly, so two rounds of seven related rows cost less than one round of fourteen unrelated ones and close more items.
lessons.apply: Cut the round by item and by file connection, with a ceiling near fourteen rows. Ask what the round CLOSES, not how many rows it touches — and if the answer is no item, say so before starting.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/followups.py bundles — the file-connected subsystem, cut by item

lessons.rule: A projection names its weakest number and refuses where it cannot measure. A figure with no stated basis is a promise.
lessons.defect: The plan's own forecaster projects about a hundred rounds to completion from an item rate measured over items ALL of which are in Phases 1 and 2, applied to phases whose work differs, while 25 of 42 open build items have never been sized by a single row. It says all of this in its own basis line, and calls the coverage figure 'the weakest number on this page'. The defect is the earlier version that did not.
lessons.apply: State the population, exclude one-time intakes and owner-switch items rather than counting them as rounds, refuse to project an item with too few observations, and say which figure you trust least. Never a date (M-MEAS-04).
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/plan_followups.py forecast() — items_basis, not_assessable_because, and the projection-coverage sentence

lessons.rule: A lesson enters the method only as a CANDIDATE, from a CONFIRMED defect, ratified by the agency that holds the method.
lessons.defect: Without it, whoever closed a row could rewrite the discipline everything else is checked against. And a lesson from an unclosed row can be fiction: W507 dropped two rows as factually wrong, and a rule derived from either would have entered the method as truth.
lessons.apply: POST /api/v1/method/derive carries the row's own measured text across as the DEFECT and refuses a row that is not `done`; it leaves the RULE to a proposer, because a sentence this code invented from a row's title is a rule nobody thought about. Change Control ratifies.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py derive_lesson() — refuses a row whose status is not done

lessons.rule: A lesson breached AGAIN is a MECHANISM failure, not a discipline failure. A rule that is broken after being written needs a tool, not a reminder.
lessons.defect: Three classes, each with a written rule already in place when it recurred. Line endings: four separate breaches across two rounds, including one heredoc that left a CRLF file mixed. A comment quoting the literal its own guard forbids: twice in one night, five red runs. Vacuous blinds: 17 of 79 in one round, 9 of 46 in another, 2 in a third — and five of the nine were a single sub-class. Each breach followed a rule that said not to.
lessons.apply: On the second breach, stop restating the rule and change the instrument: convert the check from source text to an AST or binding, move it into the pre-flight, or make the mistake impossible. Record the breach so the count can be seen (M-LEARN-03).
lessons.why_not_enforced: Nothing observes a breach. The count exists only where someone records one, which is exactly why the loop needs POST /api/v1/method/breach.

lessons.rule: Count breaches ON the lesson, and escalate on the count. The third breach of a judgement-only lesson raises a change to give it an enforcer.
lessons.defect: `why_not_enforced` was written once per lesson and never revisited, so a reason that was true when written outlived its truth — several of those reasons name tooling that has since been built. And with no count, the difference between a rule breached once and a rule breached four times is invisible, so the method cannot tell which of its own rules is failing.
lessons.apply: Record every breach against the lesson it broke. At the third breach of a lesson nothing enforces, the platform raises a Change Control candidate: give it an enforcer, or restate why none is possible now. The escalation is automatic; the answer is the agency's.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py record_breach() — writes data/method_breaches.json and raises a Change Control candidate at the third breach of an unenforced lesson

lessons.rule: Learn from what WORKED, not only from what broke. A register that ingests only failures cannot hold a practice that reduced cost.
lessons.defect: Adversarial refutation converged in EIGHT passes at W463, seven at W465 and six at W468 — a measured improvement caused by writing the invariant and the full state table FIRST, and deciding status rules from facts read at the time rather than from names or exception types. No defect would ever have produced that rule, so a failure-only register would have lost the single largest cost reduction this programme has measured.
lessons.apply: When a round costs measurably less than the last comparable one, record WHAT changed as a lesson with the measurement as its evidence — the convergence count, the round count, the wall clock. The `defect` field then holds the cost that the practice removed.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Recognising that a round went better, and why, is a judgement. Nothing compares rounds automatically, and the comparable-round question is itself a reading.

lessons.rule: Every instrument a lesson names must RESOLVE. An `enforced_by` path is a claim, and a claim about a tool is checkable.
lessons.defect: Three external assessments of this repository were verified and each had inherited stale figures from the README and inferred a destination from its adjectives; the discipline they recommended was sound and several instruments they named did not exist. The same risk is internal: a lesson whose `enforced_by` names a guard that was renamed reads as enforced and catches nothing.
lessons.apply: Resolve every named path and guard name against the tree when the method is read, and report an unresolvable one as UNENFORCED rather than as enforced. Take a lesson from an outside assessment; never take its figures or its destination.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/method_instruments.py
lessons.why_not_enforced: the PATHS and NAMES are now checked by scripts/method_instruments.py. What remains judgement is the harder half: whether the guard a lesson names would actually CATCH a breach of it, which is a reading of the guard and not of its name.

lessons.rule: A lesson derived from an UNVERIFIED claim is worse than none. A finding is a claim until something measured it.
lessons.defect: W502: a blind reported a defect that could not occur. `StoreUnavailable(path, problem)` takes two arguments, the resulting TypeError was swallowed, and the branch never ran — so the blind was vacuous and acting on it would have 'fixed' correct code. Two rows in W507 were the same shape at register level and were dropped.
lessons.apply: Before deriving anything from a finding, ask whether the EDIT produced the condition the finding describes, and whether the branch runs at all. A confirmed defect is one something drove; the rest are candidates.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py derive_lesson() — only a closed row may become a candidate

lessons.rule: A symptom is not a cause, and N symptoms are not N defects. REPRODUCE before diagnosing, and suspect one cause when the symptoms arrive together.
lessons.defect: A suite run reported FIFTY-TWO failures. They were not fifty-two defects: they were one cause — the suite's own data directory had been deleted underneath it mid-run. Proven by re-running five of the fifty-two against a fresh store, where four passed immediately. Diagnosing from the failure list would have produced fifty-two 'fixes' to code that was correct.
lessons.apply: Before reading any failure in detail, ask what the failures have in COMMON and whether the harness could have produced all of them. Re-run a small sample in a clean environment: if the sample passes, the diagnosis is about the environment and not about the code.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Nothing correlates failures by cause. A tool COULD flag that N failures share one message or one assertion line, which is what POST /api/v1/method/diagnose now does — but whether that shared signature is the cause is a reading.

lessons.rule: Bisect to the smallest reproducer FIRST. A diagnosis that costs a full verification run is one you will only make once.
lessons.defect: A guard set a field, asserted it, and a route returned None one line later. The cause was an `importlib.reload` in another test rebinding the module's singleton while the route held the instance bound when the app was built. A THREE-TEST selector reproduced it in SIXTEEN SECONDS; the full suite takes about fifty minutes. The first attempt at that diagnosis was made at full-suite scale, which is why it took the rest of the round.
lessons.apply: Find the smallest set of tests, or the smallest script, that shows the symptom, and iterate there. Measure the reproducer's cost: if it is minutes, the diagnosis will be wrong before it is right, because nobody runs a fifty-minute experiment ten times.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Choosing the reproducer is the diagnostic skill itself; no artefact records it.

lessons.rule: Ask what the EDIT produced, not what the error says. An error message can be entirely truthful and the conclusion it invites entirely wrong.
lessons.defect: Two measured cases. W502: a blind reported a defect that could not occur — `StoreUnavailable(path, problem)` takes two arguments, the resulting TypeError was swallowed, and the branch never ran; trusting the report would have 'fixed' correct code. W509: a guard's `\b` collapsed into a literal BACKSPACE character, so the check searched for a control byte and could never match — the assertion text read perfectly.
lessons.apply: Trace the condition back to the edit that was supposed to create it, and confirm the branch RUNS. If you cannot state what a user would observe, you have a symptom and not a defect.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py derive_lesson() — only a CLOSED row may become a lesson

lessons.rule: Diagnose to the CHOKEPOINT. A diagnosis that lands on a call site rather than on the default will be made again.
lessons.defect: Recall was diagnosed at the call sites twice. W488 audited `query_meta` only; `query`, `stream` and `stream_meta` still defaulted to augment=True, so TWENTY-NINE generation callers — the live nine-stage synthesis cascade, the CEO blueprint, the digital-twin modeller — still carried another request's content as analysis of their own subject. The DEFAULT was the diagnosis. Separately, a 'repo-wide' audit grepped one of four entry points and missed 29 callers of the same method.
lessons.apply: Ask where the behaviour is DECIDED, not where it is observed, and grep the CALL rather than the method name — including tests. Count the consumers before concluding the scope.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Whether a site is the chokepoint or one of many is a reading of the call graph; an import graph does not show a runtime directory scan or an infra-only reference (see [[feedback-reachability-blind-spots]]).

lessons.rule: Rule things OUT in writing, and NAME what is still unexplained. An unexplained residue stated is a diagnosis; an unexplained residue omitted is a guess.
lessons.defect: The parallel-suite stall was measured at about one run in three, with every worker in flight at once. Four hypotheses were ruled out with the evidence for each — the store lock (bounded timeout, raises, breaks a stale file), the shared register lock (deselecting all 19 subprocess tests did not change the rate), the round's own new guards (the stalls predate them), and order dependence (scatter was green on completed runs). What all workers block on at once is STILL UNEXPLAINED, and saying so is why the 4.8x speed-up was not made the default: a tool that fails silently a third of the time is the instrument-that-cannot-fail defect inverted.
lessons.apply: Write the hypothesis list, the evidence that killed each one, and the residue. Then decide what to do about the residue explicitly — including 'not adopted until explained', which is a decision and not a failure.
lessons.why_not_enforced: A ruled-out hypothesis is a written argument, not a field.

lessons.rule: Measure the RIGHT quantity. The diagnosis is often in a comparison nobody made.
lessons.defect: A night that looked like slow tests was FOUR HOURS of wall clock for 355 SECONDS of CPU. No log line said that; the diagnosis came only from comparing the two quantities, and the cause was two destroyed runs rather than slowness at all. Git's own round measurement is the same shape: a median of 4.5 hours over a 0.2-10.9 range says almost nothing until the range is read.
lessons.apply: When a symptom is 'slow', 'flaky' or 'intermittent', find two quantities whose ratio should be stable — wall clock against CPU, attempts against completions, writes against rows — and compare them. A single number rarely diagnoses anything.
lessons.enforced_by: scripts/followups.py forecast — reports wall clock with its range, separately from rates

lessons.rule: Correct FORWARD. Never remove a true statement to fix an over-claim — that trades one defect for another.
lessons.defect: W502: an over-claim was narrowed, and the narrowing killed a case where the strong statement was TRUE. The record then understated what the platform does, which is the same class of defect as overstating it and is harder to find because nobody audits for modesty.
lessons.apply: State the condition under which the strong claim holds, rather than deleting it. A claim with a stated scope is correct; a claim deleted because it was sometimes wrong is a new inaccuracy.
lessons.why_not_enforced: Whether a narrowing removed a true case is a reading of both versions.

lessons.rule: A correction must REVERSE. Capture what it replaced, or it is irreversible by construction.
lessons.defect: Before W506 a governed configuration change recorded its new value and not its old one, so nothing could undo it: `reverts_to` and `reversible` are now captured from `apply_config_change`'s own `old_value`, and `revert_immune_defence` exists because a defence the organism raises must be lowerable. A change that cannot be undone is a change nobody can afford to make, which is how a platform ends up unable to correct itself.
lessons.apply: Record the prior value at the moment of the change, from the writer that HAS it — never reconstructed afterwards. A correction whose record says only what it set is a one-way door.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/change_control.py — reverts_to / reversible captured from old_value

lessons.rule: Correct at the NARROWEST true scope. The smallest correct action is often to record what is already true — not to build.
lessons.defect: W509 measured one item's six open rows and FIVE were already satisfied; the correct action for each was to CLOSE it, not to rebuild it. Two rows in W507 were factually false and the correct action was to DROP them with the measurement that refuted them. Building any of those seven would have changed working code on a false premise — seven widenings of a fix into a rewrite, avoided only by measuring first.
lessons.apply: Ask what the smallest change is that makes the record true, and prefer it. Closing, dropping, relabelling and stating a scope are all corrections; a rewrite is the largest available and needs its own justification.
lessons.why_not_enforced: The narrowest true scope is a judgement about the code the row names.

lessons.rule: NEVER correct by weakening the check. When a guard fails, decide whether the guard or the code is wrong — and decide it from the code.
lessons.defect: W508 wrote a guard asserting that a live cascade returned ZERO findings. The cascade legitimately found something, so the guard would have pressured its own weakening at every future round; it was changed to assert that the check REPORTS, which is the thing the item actually requires. The same round had a guard that depended on ambient state — a health gate held the change first, so the field under test was never set and the leg could not fail.
lessons.apply: A failing guard is a question, not an instruction. Answer it by reading the code: if the code is right, the guard asserted the wrong thing and is REWRITTEN to assert the right one — not loosened, not deleted, not marked expected-to-fail.
lessons.why_not_enforced: A loosened assertion looks exactly like a corrected one in a diff. Only the reason distinguishes them, and the reason lives in the commit message.

lessons.rule: Apply a correction under a LOCK and atomically, or it loses the very write it is making.
lessons.defect: Three separate incidents in this repository — the ledger, the AI memory store and the accounts store — all the same class: two writers each doing load, modify, write, and the second clobbering the first. The concurrency audit reproduced about 89% recognised-revenue loss and a marketplace oversell. And on Windows the atomic replace itself raised PermissionError on 170 of 200 writes under reader contention, so atomicity needed a bounded retry before it was actually atomic.
lessons.apply: Serialise the whole load-modify-write section with `store_lock(path)` and write through `atomic_write_json`. Neither alone is sufficient: the atomic write stops a reader seeing half a file, the lock stops a writer erasing another's change.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/config.py store_lock + atomic_write_json (with the bounded replace retry)

lessons.rule: A correction names its cause and its measurement in the RECORD, or a later reader cannot tell a fix from a rewrite.
lessons.defect: A status section in one defect ledger said '5 fixed + 4 open' over a table of NINE, with one entry in neither list — it was still open, and was found only because someone re-added the table. A correction that does not say what it corrected leaves the next reader to re-derive the whole thing, and a summary nobody re-added is a claim nobody checked.
lessons.apply: Every corrective change states the defect, the measurement that established it, and what the correction does NOT cover. Then re-add the summary against the rows it summarises.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py check_change() — requires a rationale of substance and the systems the change touches, and withholds an automatic approval without them

lessons.rule: REFLECTION: read the record of what was actually DONE before forming any view of where things stand. A view formed from activity is not a view of progress.
lessons.defect: For forty-eight rounds this programme reported ten rows closed per round and read it as motion. Reflection on the record showed ZERO Phase 2 items had closed in those rounds — the activity was real and the progress was not. A reflection that counts what was TOUCHED rather than what was FINISHED produces exactly that error.
lessons.apply: Read the DONE markers, the closed rows and the rounds that produced them, from the artefacts. Separate what was touched from what was closed, and say which you are reporting.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py appraise() — the reflection faculty, read from the register and the plan

lessons.rule: REASONING: derive the ORDER from constraints, never from priority alone. An item held behind another cannot be closed by working it, however high it scores.
lessons.defect: Six Phase 2 items are held behind Phase 3 by ruling, because a membrane in front of machinery that does not run can only be verified against its absence. A schedule ordered purely by priority score would have worked all six — months of effort on items that cannot complete. And the reverse: the five-gate clearance chain was read as 'cannot refuse' when it contains five refusal branches that are UNREACHABLE because every gate consults an engine that cannot fail. Reasoning found that; reflection alone could not.
lessons.apply: Resolve the blocking order first and state it, then order the unblocked set by vision value. Name the ONE change that would move the sequence materially — for this programme, measured: a worktree per blind, because verification dominates a round's cost.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/plan_followups.py _gate_phase() — the gate phase bounds the schedule

lessons.rule: ATTRIBUTION: every claim names its PRODUCER and the round that made it. A figure with no attribution cannot be re-measured, only believed.
lessons.defect: A register row asserted '19 call sites' with no record of how it was counted; the real figure at measurement was ZERO, and the one text occurrence was inside a comment. Another asserted '52 of 61' and another '524 orphan files' where the count is now 150. Three external assessments of this repository inherited stale figures from the README and presented them as findings. None of these was dishonest; each was unattributed, so nothing could age it.
lessons.apply: Record HOW a figure was produced beside the figure — the command, the round, the tree. Then a successor re-measures instead of inheriting (M-HAND-02), and a stale figure is visible as stale rather than as false.
lessons.why_not_enforced: A register row can be required to name its source round, and is. Whether the figure in its body was measured that way is a reading of the body.

lessons.rule: RECOGNITION: name the CLASS a finding belongs to before acting on it. A finding treated as unique is fixed at its site, and a site fix is made again.
lessons.defect: Recall was fixed at the call sites TWICE before anyone recognised the class: the DEFAULT was the defect, and twenty-nine callers carried another request's content until it was recognised. A sweep for one sentence — 'the top X' resolved by insertion order — found 25 candidate sites, 9 reachable and 7 live, all one class. Recognition is what turned nineteen separate rows into seven mechanisms in the Phase 2 appraisal, which is the difference between twenty rounds and four.
lessons.apply: Ask which of the register's defect classes a finding is, and whether the mechanism that would fix it fixes others. Cut a round by MECHANISM, not by row count. Where a finding fits no class, that is a candidate for a new one — through Change Control.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py screen_for_defect_shapes() — the six classes, as shapes

lessons.rule: FORESIGHT: project in ROUNDS, from one forecaster, and name the projection's weakest input in the same breath as the number.
lessons.defect: The plan projects about a hundred rounds to completion from an item rate measured over items ALL of which are in Phases 1 and 2, applied to phases whose work differs, while twenty-five of forty-two open build items have never been sized by a single row. The defect is not the projection — it is the earlier version that reported the number without the sentence that says which figure to trust least.
lessons.apply: One forecaster, never two. State the population, exclude one-time intakes and owner switches, refuse to project what too few observations cover, and never a date.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/plan_followups.py forecast() — items_basis and not_assessable_because

lessons.rule: HINDSIGHT: check the projection's own BASIS against what happened. A rate measured on one population and applied to another is an assumption, and the assumption is testable.
lessons.defect: The item rate is computed over the whole span and applied forward — but the rate rose sharply once acceptance bars were written, because the blocker had never been the work. A projection that does not look back at whether its own rate is stable reports a smooth average over a discontinuity. Hindsight is also what catches a forecast that was right for the wrong reason: five of one item's six rows were already satisfied, so the round that 'closed' them on schedule had not done the work the schedule assumed.
lessons.apply: Compare the rate over the earlier half of the span against the later half and say whether it is stable. When a round beats its projection, ask WHY before banking it — a round that closed rows nobody had to build is a measurement finding, not velocity.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py appraise() — the hindsight faculty compares the two halves of the span

lessons.rule: INTROSPECTION: state what the platform's own record CANNOT see. A platform that reports only what it holds is grading its own homework.
lessons.defect: Forty-six of seventy-nine method rules are enforced by nothing and each had to be made to SAY so, because a method presented as enforced is a compliance badge. Twenty-five of forty-two open build items have never been sized. A breach count of zero means no breach was RECORDED, and nothing observes a breach. Every one of those was, at some point, reported as a clean figure.
lessons.apply: Report the unenforced share, the unsized share and the unobserved share as first-class figures beside the confident ones. 'Not assessable' is an answer and usually the honest one (M-VERIF-10).
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py _enforcement_summary() — the enforced share, stated

lessons.rule: EXTROSPECTION: read the TREE, not the record, before believing the record. The record is a claim about the world; the world is checkable.
lessons.defect: Three consecutive rounds of measured evidence. W507 DROPPED two rows as factually false — the script they accused walks no such path. W508 found two already satisfied and one three-quarters done. W509 measured one item's six open rows and FIVE were already satisfied by earlier rounds. The following appraisal found four more, one of which was the BLOCKING row of the item it rode. Roughly nine of every fifteen rows examined needed no build at all — and every one of them was believed until the tree was read.
lessons.apply: Before scheduling a row, read the code it names and record what is there. A row measured false is DROPPED with the measurement that refutes it; a row already satisfied is CLOSED. Both are appraisal work. Where the tree has moved under a row since the round that found it, that row is a CANDIDATE for re-reading — never an automatic close, because whether a row is satisfied is a reading of code and not a diff.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py appraise() — the extrospection faculty lists rows whose files the tree changed after the round that found them

lessons.rule: RETROSPECTION: read the record for its PATTERN, not its totals. A count says what happened; a pattern says what keeps happening.
lessons.defect: The register's totals said 'rows are closing steadily'. The pattern said something else entirely: across three consecutive rounds, roughly NINE of the fifteen rows examined needed no build at all — two were factually false, seven were already satisfied by an earlier round and had never been closed. The totals could not show that, because a row closed because it was satisfied and a row closed because it was built are the same increment. The pattern is computable — dropped and already-satisfied closes against built ones — and nobody computed it for forty-eight rounds.
lessons.apply: Compute the shape of the record: the refutation share (rows DROPPED as false against rows closed), rounds that only FOUND against rounds that CLOSED, and whether the found rate is outrunning the closed rate. Then say what it means — a high refutation share means the register OVER-STATES the work (M-FCAST-02), and that is a finding about the register, not about the code.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py appraise() — the retrospection faculty

lessons.rule: OBSERVATION: read what is happening NOW, from the live system, before inferring anything about it. Inference without observation is the most expensive habit available.
lessons.defect: THIS SESSION, five times. (1) I proposed building a metabolic budget; the mechanism already existed, fully wired, and two coefficients made it inert. (2) I proposed a mutual-aid channel; investment between entities was already built and a rescue channel would have corrupted the stage it reused. (3) I proposed importing 'the real HomeostaticRegulator'; it is not a controller — its integral term is never accumulated. (4) and (5) I 'fixed' two event shapes that were not broken, and both fixes failed the suite: one re-pointed a field's type and raised `unhashable type: 'dict'`, the other reclassified a framing event and double-counted a call. Every one was a surface read, a gap inferred, a build proposed. In not one case was the live state read first.
lessons.apply: Before proposing anything: read the live state — is the beat running, what did it last do, what is in flight, what does the surface actually return when called. A reading of NOW is stale the moment it is taken, and it says so; that is still infinitely better than an inference with no reading behind it.
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py appraise() — the observation faculty

lessons.rule: PROSPECTION: enumerate what COULD happen and refuse to rank it. A possibility given a probability has been turned into a prediction, and this platform has exactly one forecaster.
lessons.defect: The plan could say how many rounds its measured rate projects, and could say nothing at all about what would become possible if the gate cleared, or what either answer to an Owner decision opens. Six Phase 2 items are held behind eight Phase 3 items and that branch was readable the whole time — but only as prose in an item body, never as a structure anything could compute. A plan that can extrapolate one line and cannot enumerate its branches presents a single future as the only one.
lessons.apply: List the branches with the ASSUMPTION each rests on: what unblocks if a gate clears, what each answer to an open decision makes possible. Label every one a POSSIBILITY. Never a probability, never a ranking, never a date — those belong to the one forecaster, and a second voice on the same question is two records disagreeing (M-DELIV-08).
lessons.enforced_by: agentic_core/api/method.py appraise() — the prospection faculty

lessons.rule: A claim that the method itself is trustworthy must be tested, or not made. Corroboration requires DISJOINT samples; two nested windows agreeing is evidence of nothing.
lessons.defect: W514: session_forecast.py and OVERNIGHT_METHOD.md both stated 'two independent windows agreeing within 0.06h is the reason this is usable at all'. W490+ is a SUBSET of W460+ (10 of 30 samples are the same data), so the windows were neither independent nor corroborating, and the agreement was near-tautological. The claim was load-bearing: it was offered as the reason to trust the figure a commitment was then built on.
lessons.apply: State the estimator and its sample once. To corroborate, split the history into DISJOINT halves and compare; report the difference. Run that test before citing agreement as evidence. (Run afterwards for W449+: first half median 1.97h, second half 2.43h, differing by 0.46h — the figure IS corroborated, but by this test and not by the nested one originally cited.)
lessons.why_not_enforced: a guard can assert that two compared windows do not overlap, but it cannot tell whether a prose sentence is claiming corroboration; the durable fix is that no figure is restated in prose at all (M-SESS-02)

lessons.rule: A measured figure appears in exactly one place — the code that computes it. It is never typed into prose, and a document that needs it prints it by running the instrument.
lessons.defect: W514: the suite cost was written as both 0.90h and 0.91h (two scripts holding the same constant differently: 3274/3600 against (3274+3200)/2/3600); its share of a round as both 41% and 43%; the selector ratio as 65x when a realistic 2-4 test selector measures 19-24x; and 'one night in seven' where the committed band was 90% (one in ten). Four of nine self-audit findings and several audit findings were this single class, in documents that themselves state 'import the constant, never restate it'.
lessons.apply: One shared constants module, imported. Method documents carry zero numbers and point at the generator. If a figure must appear in prose, it is generated into that prose at render time or it does not appear.
lessons.enforced_by: integration_tests/test_mvp_spine.py::test_w514_the_method_documents_carry_no_measured_figures

lessons.rule: An exclusion must justify itself against the population it excluded — not merely state its rule. Report what was dropped and why each dropped item qualifies.
lessons.defect: W514: the capacity instruments dropped every round-to-round gap over 5h as 'containing idle', justified by the true principle that an interval is not a duration, and reported only the COUNT (19). Tested afterwards, 6 of those 19 were daytime gaps — plausibly long rounds, not sleep. Restoring them moved P(>=2 rounds) from 91% to 75% and the committed count from 2 to 1. The filter could not report that it had discarded real rounds, because nothing looked: an instrument that cannot fail, one level up from the test.
lessons.apply: Every filter reports its excluded items individually with the property that justified exclusion (here: whether the gap spans 03-06 UTC). A filtered population stated as a bare count is not an honest population.
lessons.why_not_enforced: NOT YET ENFORCED — the guard described here is not written, and naming an absent instrument is the defect this register warns about. It would assert: a guard driving a filter with a known-misclassifiable item and asserting the report names it and its reason

lessons.rule: The committed figure comes from ONE rule, in code. A mechanism whose headline output is routinely overridden in prose is not a mechanism.
