lessons.defect: W514: session_forecast.py returned committed_round_count = 1 by taking the minimum of two windows' p75 bands, and the documents said 'I am overriding it to 2 as a judgement call'. Compounding two conservative estimates produced a number nobody used, while the prose figure carried the authority of having been 'measured'.
lessons.apply: One rule decides the commitment — the simulation's >=85% band. Any other computed count is named for what it is (worst_case_round_count) so it cannot be read as the commitment. If judgement overrides the rule, the override is recorded as a variance with its reason, not as the figure.
lessons.why_not_enforced: NOT YET ENFORCED — the guard described here is not written, and naming an absent instrument is the defect this register warns about. It would assert: a guard asserting exactly one field in the capacity output is named as the commitment

lessons.rule: A probability about SELF is a measurement; a probability about another's decision is a fabrication. Never rank branches that turn on what the Owner or another agent will choose.
lessons.defect: W514: the capacity mechanism attaches probabilities to possibilities, which is exactly what api/method.py _prospect() refuses to do — 'ranked by nothing, ever; a possibility given a probability has been turned into a prediction'. Bolting the simulation into prospection would have broken a designed invariant QUIETLY, because the function would still have returned branches.
lessons.apply: Capacity is a separate faculty answering only about this system's own throughput. Prospection may consume it as a stated assumption while continuing to enumerate rather than rank.
lessons.why_not_enforced: NOT YET ENFORCED — the guard described here is not written, and naming an absent instrument is the defect this register warns about. It would assert: the existing prospection guard, plus a guard asserting the capacity faculty's output contains no branch about an Owner decision

lessons.rule: Capacity is an INPUT to a plan, not something the plan measures. Say so where the plan is read.
lessons.defect: W514: remaining allowance is readable only through the host application, never from a script, so an unattended plan rests on a number it cannot verify. A plan that buried that assumption would be confidently wrong whenever the hours were wrong.
lessons.apply: The generated plan states at the top that capacity is an input and that everything below is void if the hours are wrong.
lessons.why_not_enforced: the value arrives from outside the repository; the guard can only assert the disclosure sentence is present, which is prose-checking and therefore weak

lessons.rule: Amortise one full verification over several COHERENT changes, bounded by the attribution test: if a red suite could not be attributed to one batched change within one diagnosis pass, the batch was too big.
lessons.defect: W514 measured the full suite at a fixed ~0.9h and 42% of a median round, with a realistic diff-scoped selector 19-24x faster. Small-batch guidance (DORA) and that fixed cost point opposite ways, and collapsing one into the other loses either attribution or throughput.
lessons.apply: Selector first on the diff, one full suite last on the final tree, with the process exit code captured explicitly. Batch only changes in one subsystem or one defect class.
lessons.why_not_enforced: NOT YET ENFORCED — the guard described here is not written, and naming an absent instrument is the defect this register warns about. It would assert: the existing round rhythm plus the requirement that a round's commit lists its files explicitly

lessons.rule: An unattended session spends one error budget: a single red-suite re-run. A second red suite stops the session; it does not buy a third attempt.
lessons.defect: W514: a red suite cost a full 53-minute re-verification, which is 11% of an 8-hour night. Without a stated budget an unattended session can spend the whole night re-running the same failure, and W498-W500 record three instruments that reported success while doing nothing for hours.
lessons.apply: Reserve one suite duration as contingency. On a red suite take one diagnosis pass; if it does not resolve, stop, write it up, leave the tree clean.
lessons.why_not_enforced: the budget governs the session's own conduct rather than a code property; it is checkable only in the night report, which is why the report is written before capacity ends

lessons.rule: Do not start a round that cannot finish in the time remaining. A half-built round leaves a tree someone else must untangle; an early finish only means pulling the next item forward.
lessons.defect: W514: the p75 round duration is materially longer than the median (4.10h against 2.09h), so a plan sized on the median starts rounds it cannot land roughly a quarter of the time.
lessons.apply: Compare time remaining against p75, not the median, before starting. Checkpoint granularity is one round to one commit, so an abandoned round costs at most itself.
lessons.why_not_enforced: NOT YET ENFORCED — the guard described here is not written, and naming an absent instrument is the defect this register warns about. It would assert: a guard asserting the generated plan states a p75-based do-not-start threshold

lessons.rule: A commitment is recorded with its confidence where a reader meets it, and its variance is recorded when the session ends. A promise with no variance cannot improve.
lessons.defect: W514 measured (recursively, at every depth) that no commitment, confidence, variance, budget or capacity field exists in the Change Control record, the queue, GET /cca/{id} or the transformation cycle — so Workstation can govern a change but cannot record what scope was promised, at what confidence, against what capacity, nor what actually happened. Registered as FU-313.
lessons.apply: The transformation cycle carries a commitment; the session's variance feeds the next capacity measurement. Until FU-313 lands, the commitment lives in the generated plan and the variance in the night report, and both say they are not yet held by the platform.
lessons.why_not_enforced: the field does not exist yet; FU-313 is the build, and the guard belongs with it

lessons.rule: Nothing heavy runs beside the suite. Not a second suite, and not an agent fleet: the suite is a wall-clock instrument and contention makes its timing-sensitive tests lie.
lessons.defect: W515: an adversarial verification workflow - 48 agents, 741 tool uses, 3.5M subagent tokens - was launched on the same machine as a running full suite. The suite took 1h48m34s against its measured 53m20s, a 2.04x slowdown, and returned RED on exactly two tests, both timing or process sensitive: test_store_lock_serialises_across_processes and test_cross_tenant_isolation_under_auth. Neither was in the round's blast radius (the round touched vbs/quality.py, compliance/ethical_engine.py, docs and the register). Re-run in isolation on a quiet machine both passed in 81s. So the round's only red was self-inflicted by the session's own concurrency, and an hour of verification had to be paid twice. The existing rule covered 'never two pytest suites at once' because two suites corrupt shared stores; it did not cover a fleet, whose damage is to TIMING rather than to data, and which therefore looks like a real defect instead of an obvious collision.
lessons.apply: Before starting a full suite, confirm no workflow, refuter fleet, blind sweep or other multi-process work is running, and start none until it lands. If a suite returns red on a timing or process sensitive test while other work was running, the FIRST diagnosis step is to re-run those tests alone on a quiet machine - and the outcome of that re-run does not authorise a commit, because a passing subset is a hypothesis and the full suite is the verdict. Re-run the full suite clean.
lessons.why_not_enforced: NOT YET ENFORCED - a guard would have to observe sibling processes at suite start, which is ambient-environment observation and the M-VERIF-02 class. The honest mechanism is procedural: the round's own pre-flight asks the question, and the suite's wall-clock is compared against the measured constant in scripts/_session_measured.py, where a run materially slower than SUITE_H is evidence of contention rather than of a defect.

mechanisms.name: Priority scoring, per-item pace, and class batches
mechanisms.what: Open rows are scored by vision value (docs/PRIORITY.json) and the schedule is ordered by it. The pace is measured from the register and projected in rounds. Rounds are proposed as a file-connected subsystem cut by item, or as the class one mechanism closes.
mechanisms.known_limit: The batch generator cannot see a row that cites no defect class.

mechanisms.name: Acceptance bars, and progress measured in rounds
mechanisms.what: An item closes on its ACCEPT criteria. The plan measures its own pace from the register, projects in ROUNDS and never dates, excludes one-time sweeps by name, refuses to project an item too few of whose rows have closed, and names the weakest figure on the page.
mechanisms.known_limit: 25 of 42 build items have never been sized, so the item projection is an average over a population most of which no round has measured. It says so.

mechanisms.name: The round rhythm
mechanisms.what: Read the batch → measure each row's LIVE state → patch → mechanical pre-flight → guard test → blind harness with asserted byte-restore → refute the round's own diff → register and render → one full suite on the final tree → commit with an explicit file list → push → check CI → update the method and the memory.
mechanisms.known_limit: Nothing enforces the order; a round that skips the blind sweep produces the same artefacts as one that ran it.

mechanisms.name: Pre-flight, blind harness, adversarial refutation, three-state verdicts
mechanisms.what: A mechanical pre-flight over the diff checks the deterministic defect shapes. A blind harness breaks each guard's subject and requires it to go red, separating BAD BLIND from VACUOUS. An adversarial pass refutes the round's own fixes in isolated worktrees. Verdicts are three-state with a basis.
mechanisms.known_limit: The pre-flight covers seven deterministic shapes (keys, renames, routes, returns, selfmatch, banned, order). The largest labelled class — a new claim the code cannot back — is NOT covered; FU-262 proposes extending it.

mechanisms.name: The follow-up register
mechanisms.what: Every found-but-not-done task is a row carrying what was measured, why it matters and which plan item owns it, added in the same commit and routed to an item by file and word. A row closes only when every finding in it is fixed; an item cannot be marked done while a row rides it.
mechanisms.known_limit: A row's own text can go stale, and a row may accuse working code — two were dropped as false in W507.

mechanisms.name: Preparation: measure, then draft
mechanisms.what: A round is prepared by MEASURING each candidate row's live state, drafting each patch as a script whose anchors are asserted and whose needles carry the target's line endings, writing any missing ACCEPT bar from the item's own deliverables, and naming what the round will not do. Preparation happens during another round's verification, read-only.
mechanisms.known_limit: Nothing enforces that a row's live state was measured, and a prepared patch can still be applied to a tree that moved under it - the anchors are what catch that.

mechanisms.name: Handover: the artefacts, not the narration
mechanisms.what: What survives a context is the register (docs/FOLLOWUPS.json), the plan (docs/FABLE_DELIVERY_PROMPT.md), this method, and the memory. A handover states the verified, the unverified, the measured-but-unexplained and the deliberately-excluded, carries the measurement rather than the conclusion, and slots every open decision to the Owner. GET /api/v1/method/handover computes the current state from those artefacts rather than narrating it.
mechanisms.known_limit: It can count what the artefacts hold; it cannot tell that something was never written down. An unrecorded decision is invisible to it by construction, which is why M-HAND-01 is a rule and not a report.

mechanisms.name: Forecasting: two rates, measured in rounds, with the weakest number named
mechanisms.what: ONE forecaster, `agentic_core/plan_followups.forecast()`, reached by `scripts/followups.py forecast` and `GET /api/v1/plan/followups`. It measures the ROW rate over build rounds (rounds that closed something — a sweep adds work, it does not burn it), the ITEM rate over the whole span because a six-round window cannot measure something that takes many rounds, excludes one-time intakes and owner-switch items rather than counting them as rounds, refuses to project an item with too few observations, and reports wall clock from git as a separate measurement with its range. `GET /api/v1/method/forecast` reads it and adds only what arithmetic cannot know: that the open-row count is an upper bound (M-FCAST-02), that verification dominates the cost (M-FCAST-03), and which items are blocked by ruling (M-FCAST-05).
mechanisms.known_limit: 25 of 42 open build items have never been sized by a row, so the item projection is an average over a population most of which no round has measured — its own basis calls this the weakest number on the page. It is arithmetic over an observed mean in ROUNDS: never a date, and it moves every time a round closes or registers a row.

mechanisms.name: Learning: a defect becomes a rule, a repeat becomes a tool
mechanisms.what: The loop that makes this register live. A CONFIRMED defect (a closed register row) becomes a CANDIDATE lesson through POST /api/v1/method/derive, which carries the row's own measured text as the defect and refuses an open row; Change Control ratifies, because the agency that checks changes against the method also owns it. A breach of an existing lesson is recorded through POST /api/v1/method/breach, which counts breaches on the lesson and, at the THIRD breach of a lesson nothing enforces, raises a Change Control candidate to give it an enforcer or restate why none is possible. Successes enter the same way, with the measurement as evidence (M-LEARN-04).
mechanisms.known_limit: Nothing detects an UNRECORDED breach, so the loop turns only when someone records one — which is the honest reason most of this method is still judgement rather than enforcement. The escalation raises a change; it cannot write the enforcer.

mechanisms.name: Diagnosis: reproduce small, rule out in writing, name the residue
mechanisms.what: The step between a symptom and a patch, which this register had no rules for at all. Reproduce before diagnosing and suspect ONE cause when symptoms arrive together; bisect to the smallest reproducer and measure its cost; trace the condition back to the edit that was meant to create it; diagnose to the chokepoint rather than the call site; write the hypotheses you ruled out with the evidence, and name what is still unexplained. POST /api/v1/method/diagnose screens a set of observed failures for a SHARED SIGNATURE — the shape that says one cause rather than N defects — and lists what must be ruled out before anything is changed.
mechanisms.known_limit: It can see that failures SHARE a signature; it cannot tell that the signature is the cause, and it cannot see a single failure's cause at all. A shared signature is a reason to re-run a sample in a clean environment, never a diagnosis.

mechanisms.name: Correction: forward, narrowest, reversible, and recorded
mechanisms.what: Correct FORWARD by stating a scope rather than deleting a true claim; take the NARROWEST true action, which is often to close or drop a row rather than build; never weaken a failing check — rewrite it to assert the right thing; apply the change under store_lock and atomically, because both are needed; and state the cause, the measurement and what the correction does not cover. POST /api/v1/method/correct assesses a proposed correction against those five, three-state, and submits it to Change Control when asked — the agency that holds the method also owns the corrections made against it.
mechanisms.known_limit: Four of the five are judgements. It can check that a prior value was captured and that the record states a cause; it cannot tell a loosened assertion from a corrected one, because in a diff they look identical and only the reason distinguishes them.

mechanisms.name: The Appraisal Cell: eight faculties, four paired axes
mechanisms.what: A reusable UNIT rather than a list of rules. Given a scope — a phase, an item, a set of rows — the cell takes eight readings and reconciles them: REFLECTION on what was actually finished and REASONING about what follows from the constraints; ATTRIBUTION of every figure to its producer and RECOGNITION of the class it belongs to; FORESIGHT in rounds from the one forecaster and HINDSIGHT on whether that forecaster's own rate is stable; INTROSPECTION on what the record cannot see and EXTROSPECTION on what only the tree can tell us. Neither end of any axis is sufficient alone: reflection without reasoning is a diary, foresight without hindsight is a promise, and introspection without extrospection is a platform grading its own homework. GET /api/v1/method/appraise runs the cell; the Transformation Office may appraise a transformation's scope with it, and Change Control may appraise a change's before deciding. W512 — the cell also carries a TEMPORAL SPINE of three, because time is not a dyad: RETROSPECTION reads the record for its pattern, OBSERVATION reads the live state now, and PROSPECTION enumerates branches without ranking them. The middle term is the one the cell was built without, and the cost of its absence is recorded in M-APPR-10's defect: five proposals in one session that a single reading of the live state would have prevented. Retrospection without observation is nostalgia; prospection without observation is fantasy; observation without either is drift.
mechanisms.known_limit: Two of the eight faculties are largely judgement and say so: ATTRIBUTION can require a row to name its source round but cannot tell whether the figure in its body was measured that way, and REASONING can report the blocking order the plan states but cannot discover a constraint nobody wrote down. EXTROSPECTION reports CANDIDATES for re-reading and never closes a row: whether a row is satisfied is a reading of code, not a diff — and where git history is unavailable it reports that rather than an empty list. PROSPECTION is the most easily abused faculty in the cell: it enumerates branches and must never rank them or attach a likelihood, because that is the forecaster's job and there is only one forecaster. OBSERVATION is stale the instant it is read, and says so.

defect_classes.name: A result reported where nothing discriminated
defect_classes.shape: A value SELECTED or REPORTED as a result when nothing actually discriminated; a constant presented as a measurement; or a field whose NAME implies a determination the value cannot support.
defect_classes.how_to_find: `max(` or `min(` over a mapping, a `sort` then `[0]`, or a loop returning the first item clearing a threshold — over data where TIES are the normal condition, such as small integer counts or dict keys inserted in a fixed order.
defect_classes.why_it_is_severe: It moves real decisions. One instance credited a model for a cascade verdict, which moves routing; another decided rejected-versus-held in governance.
defect_classes.measured: 9 of 9 audited native-AI primitives carried it (docs/NATIVE_PRIMITIVE_DEFECT_LEDGER.md); a later sweep of the shapes above across agentic_core gave 25 candidates, 9 reachable, 7 live defects — every one the same sentence, 'the top X' resolved by insertion order.
defect_classes.the_fix: Disclose the tie and carry its magnitude: name every tied leader, or return null with a `*_tied` field beside it. Where a tie must not arise, remove the SITUATION rather than resolve it — one live record per action under a lock, ordered by a real timestamp.

defect_classes.name: A value a reader would take as measured that nothing measures
defect_classes.shape: Any value a user or API consumer would reasonably read as measured, derived or certified, that nothing measures, derives or certifies.
defect_classes.how_to_find: A five-area sweep followed by an adversarial DEFENCE pass, ordered by reach.
defect_classes.not_this_class: configuration constants · clearly-labelled fallbacks · test fixtures · archived files · honest empty states · prompt and example text. Eleven of 70 proposals were defended on exactly these grounds (M-VERIF-12).
defect_classes.the_fix: Report what was done, or say it was not done. Never a figure with no producer.

defect_classes.name: A control that fabricates its own success
defect_classes.shape: A handler that makes no backend call and then renders success — a setTimeout followed by a prepended PASSED row with a random hash, a vote that increments local state, a provision step that sleeps and invents an id.
defect_classes.how_to_find: A handler with no fetch on its path, or one whose state update does not depend on a response. `Math.random()` or `new Date()` inside a success path is the tell.
defect_classes.why_it_is_severe: It is the honesty violation in its purest form: the user is told something happened.
defect_classes.measured: One of five clusters in docs/FRONTEND_DEFECT_LEDGER.md; all 47 seeded findings closed.
defect_classes.the_fix: Wire it, or remove the control and say what is not available.

defect_classes.name: A reader reading a key the writer never sends
defect_classes.shape: A surface reads `data.entries` where the handler returns `changes`; a status map keyed on uppercase where the server sends lowercase; a filter comparing against a value that never occurs; an id read from a field named differently on the wire.
defect_classes.how_to_find: A METHOD-AWARE diff of every call site against every handler's method+route pair — 170 UI calls against 459 backend pairs found exactly one missing endpoint and zero method mismatches, which is the finding: the breakage was all in the shapes.
defect_classes.why_it_is_severe: It renders as an empty state, so it reads as 'nothing has happened yet' rather than as a fault. One instance left the Change Control Agency page permanently empty with all four stat tiles at zero however many changes existed.
defect_classes.the_fix: Lock the shape in a guard proven to fail when the shape is broken.

defect_classes.name: A failure the user never sees
defect_classes.shape: No `res.ok` check, or an empty catch, on a user action; an error body rendered as a result.
defect_classes.how_to_find: Every call site's response handling, and every catch block with no user-visible effect.
defect_classes.the_fix: A failed action says it failed, in the place the user acted.

defect_classes.name: A raw link out of an authenticated surface
defect_classes.shape: A plain anchor or new-tab navigation to a route that depends on the current user: the navigation carries no Authorization header, so the tab shows a 401 body.
defect_classes.how_to_find: Every `<a href>` and `window.open` whose target is an API route — cross-checked against whether that route depends on the user.
defect_classes.why_it_is_severe: It is invisible while authentication is off, and every such control dead-ends the moment it is on.
defect_classes.the_fix: Fetch with the bearer and hand the user a blob, or serve the route without the dependency.
